links.outcome: Saliency map overlap (IoU, pointing game) with radiologist annotations in correctly classified chest X-rays
links.effect: 83.0% of correct predictions were dangerous failures (confidence >0.5, IoU <0.1); mean IoU 0.044 (LIME) to 0.062 (Integrated Gradients); pointing game accuracy 1.2% to 27.4%.
links.quote: we find that 83.0% of correct predictions constitute dangerous failures — cases where model confidence exceeds 0.5 yet saliency map overlap with radiologist-annotated ground truth falls below IoU = 0.1.

unlisted_practices: Establish quantitative minimum saliency localization thresholds as mandatory validation gates before deploying saliency-augmented imaging AI

screen.reason: Evaluates the spatial localization accuracy and failure rates of standard explainability/saliency map methods (GradCAM, LIME, etc.) on chest X-ray predictions, showing that high prediction accuracy decouples from explanation fidelity and suggesting validation gates.
